ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, officers, UBOs, authorized signatories, and counterparties against: (i) FINTRAC's politically exposed persons (PEP) definition, including foreign and domestic PEPs, family members, and close associates; (ii) OFAC SDN and sanctions lists (for USD clearing and correspondent banking); (iii) UN Security Council Sanctions Consolidated List; (iv) Canadian sanctions under the Special Economic Measures Act (S.C. 1992, c. 17), the United Nations Act (R.S.C., 1985, c. U-2), and the Freezing Assets of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act; and (v) Alberta corporate registry disqualification/restricted director lists. A positive PEP or sanctions hit requires enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds/source-of-wealth documentation, senior-management approval, and potential filing with FINTRAC. Additional end-use/end-user review applies under the Export and Import Permits Act for medical imaging equipment.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) – online via the Corporate Registry eService Portal or through an authorized Alberta registry agent
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A corporate name may be in English or French and must be expressed in letters A–Z, numerals 0–9 and limited punctuation; transliteration of a foreign script must be submitted with a certified English/French version. Under the ABCA and Alberta name rules, the name must be distinctive, not misleading, not contrary to public interest, and must include a legal element (Inc., Corp., Ltd., etc.). The NUANS search report examines sound, sight, and phonetic equivalences of transliterated names.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Director rejects a proposed name, the applicant may submit a written reconsideration request to the Director/Commissioner of the Alberta Corporate Registry within 30 days of the rejection, stating grounds and supplying a fresh NUANS report where applicable; the request is processed under the ABCA and registry policy, with a fee payable for reconsideration. If reconsideration is refused, the applicant may appeal to the Court of King's Bench of Alberta by originating application within the applicable limitation period. A name reservation may be extended only by filing a new/updated NUANS search before expiry of the 90-day window; no administrative extension beyond that period is available.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is generally permissible for the Alberta registered-office and records-address requirements if it provides a physical street address in Alberta, accepts service during ordinary business hours, and the corporation maintains the mandated corporate records. For this medical-device manufacturing/export scope, however, Health Canada establishment-licence conditions under the Medical Devices Regulations require a physical Canadian establishment for import/manufacture activities (warehouse, label, quality, complaint handling), so a virtual office alone will not satisfy commercial-substance expectations.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (~5%) that Alberta registry will physically inspect the registered office on an unannounced basis; elevated (~35–45%) that Health Canada, Canada Border Services Agency, or the Canada Revenue Agency will conduct an on-site establishment/audit for a medical-device manufacturer-exporter, particularly during licence renewal or first-time establishment review.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), R.S.A. 2000, c. B-9, sections 8–23 (incorporation), 22 (registered office), 103 and 106 (directors and officers), and 213 (remedies); incorporated under Alberta provincial law.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction, Government of Alberta.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form AB-1) filed with the Alberta Corporate Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for an Alberta Business Corporation. Share capital may be nominal; funds can be placed in a lawyer’s trust escrow pending completion of incorporation and opening of bank accounts. Alberta BCA does not require shareholder capital to be paid into a designated escrow account but imposes disclosure obligations for beneficial ownership under the Business Corporations Act and anti-money-laundering regulations.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the incorporation of the Corporation be and hereby is confirmed, and that the share subscription of each initial subscriber as disclosed in the Articles of Incorporation be accepted and duly allocated. RESOLVED, that the registered office be established at the address recorded in the statute office declaration, and that the corporate records be maintained at that office. RESOLVED, that [Name] be appointed President, [Name] be appointed Secretary, and [Name] be appointed Treasurer, each to serve until successors are elected. RESOLVED, that the officers be authorized to execute all regulatory filings, open banking accounts, and secure any licenses required for the Corporation’s medical imaging production activities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry — Name Search and Reservation Service via NUANS
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name request to the Alberta Corporate Registry using an authorized NUANS provider. Include the legal element and a concise business purpose. Obtain the NUANS report as evidence of name availability and reserve the name for a 90-day validity period.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name request is rejected, file a new reservation using acceptable alternates or write to the registry to contest a close similarity decision; the resubmission is treated as a new application and no separate priority right is lost.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Filing of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry — Online Incorporation Portal and authorized service agents
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form AB-1 in its entirety, specifying authorized share capital, initial directors, and the registered office address. Affix signatures of incorporators, witness if applicable, and submit either through the online portal or by mail to the registry. Pay the applicable filing fee. The registry will verify the NUANS report and officers’ consents.
required_dossiers: Consent of each initial director (Form BC-2 or equivalent)
Notice of registered office / address for service
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a query, amend the articles in response to the notice and resubmit. Withdrawal of a defective filing can be done by written request; the application will be converted to a new filing with a fresh certificate date upon cure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Public Registry Update
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After approval and issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation, file the Notice of Directors and Notice of Registered Office with the registry to update the public register. Obtain certified copies for banking, land registration, and licensing purposes.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate is not issued within the service standard, call the registry to verify the completeness of the file. Any typographical errors discovered in the issued certificate are cured by filing a Corrected Articles or Articles of Amendment under the Business Corporations Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (Business Registration Online) and Alberta Finance — Alberta Corporate Tax
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain a Federal Business Number (BN) using the CRA online portal and select the required program accounts: corporate income tax (RC), Payroll (RP), GST/HST (RT) only if taxable supply threshold exceeded, and import/export (RM). The Alberta corporate income-tax registration is completed concurrently through the CRA or the Alberta Corporate Tax portal.
required_dossiers: Corporate jurisdiction and registered office address
Legal name, civic address, and fiscal year-end of the corporation
Directors' full legal names, residency, and business contact details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the BN is not issued within 21 calendar days, contact CRA Business Enquiries and provide the Certificate of Incorporation and the completed Business Registration form. The registry will correct director information and issue a revised notice of assessment for any tax account errors.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business and Development License Authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: City of Calgary / City of Edmonton Planning and Development (or relevant municipal service commission based on registered office)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a municipal business licence for medical-device manufacturing and confirm that the proposed premises are zoned for light industrial use. Submit a development permit application if the facility requires major interior fit-out or exterior alteration to accommodate clean-room or laboratory functions for phased-array ultrasound console assembly.
required_dossiers: Development permit application (if construction or alteration)
Building and fire safety floor plan
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the business licence is refused based on zoning, apply for a discretionary use approval or minor variance before the municipal subdivision and development appeal board. If the development permit is refused, submit an amended site and building plan addressing the municipality's stated fire and building safety objections.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Health Canada, Health Products and Food Branch (medical device establishment licensing), in coordination with Alberta Labour and Immigration (occupational health and safety) and Alberta Environment and Protected Areas (industrial environmental compliance)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Medical Device Establishment Licence (MDEL) issued under the Canadian Food and Drugs Act and Medical Devices Regulations, authorizing packaging, labelling, importation, and distribution of a class II/III phased-array colour Doppler ultrasound console; supplemented by an Alberta municipal industrial business licence for assembly operations.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B Registration under the Activities Designation Regulation (A.D.R.); no full Environmental Impact Assessment required for light electronic assembly of medical imaging consoles, unless stationary combustion or solvent discharge exceeds the registration thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges must meet the Alberta Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act general requirements, municipal sewer bylaws, and Canadian Council of Ministers of Environment (CCME) water-quality guidelines. Volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions must comply with the Alberta Ambient Air Quality Objectives and CCME national ambient-air standards; all hazardous wastes (e.g., soldering residues, cleaning solvents) must be classified, manifested, and sent to an approved industrial waste facility.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety clearance by the Alberta Fire Commissioner and local municipal fire department confirming compliance with fire prevention and building code requirements. Structural load approval received from the municipal authority under the Alberta Building Code for the intended machinery and equipment loads. Occupational health and safety clearance issued by Alberta Labour and Immigration covering electrical safety, ventilation for soldering areas, noise exposure, lifting, and workstation ergonomics for assembly staff.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada — registration and filing administered through Business Registration Online (BRO) and the CRA 'My Business Account' portal (canada.ca); customs export administration: Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) via the Canadian Single Window / Canadian Export Reporting System (G-13); Alberta provincial corporate registry: Alberta Registries (Alberta Corporate Registration System), which transmits corporate identity data to the CRA.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Alberta Business Corporation obtains its statutory tax identity as follows: (1) incorporate under the Alberta Business Corporations Act or register the federal corporation as an extra-provincial company in Alberta; (2) obtain the corporate registration number from the Alberta Corporate Registry; (3) apply to the CRA for the 9-digit Business Number (BN) and the Goods and Services Tax/Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST) account (RT) through BRO or by filing Form RC1 (Request for Business Number Registration); (4) open the CBSA Import-Export (RM) account so that future export declarations for the medical ultrasound consoles can be transmitted through the G-13 Canadian Export Reporting System; (5) for a non-resident corporation, designate a Canadian representative and follow the ETA s.240(1) non-resident registration path, including the deemed-residency rule where applicable; (6) elect the GST/HST reporting period and fiscal year-end at registration; (7) verify the registration by searching the CRA GST/HST Registry.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: a federal/Alberta Business Corporation (Inc./Corp.) is an independent taxpayer under both the Income Tax Act (ITA) and the Excise Tax Act (ETA); no pass-through treatment applies to the corporation; the Alberta permanent establishment is subject to Alberta corporate income tax at 8% in addition to the federal corporate rate (as applicable), while GST/HST is administered federally at the entity level.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not maintain a US-style check-the-box election; corporate classification follows legal central management and control and the written constitutional documents. Relevant statutory elections for this exporter include: (a) the ETA s.156 joint election to treat taxable supplies between closely related corporations as made for no consideration, simplifying intercompany export-related flows; (b) the ETA s.273 election for a qualifying non-resident registrant to self-assess and claim rebates of GST/HST paid on Canadian goods and services; (c) the ITA s.93(1) foreign affiliate election for capital-gain purging where a foreign sales subsidiary is used; (d) Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) status and Small Business Deduction elections made on the T2 Schedule 17 where the ownership and control tests are met; (e) hybrid-mismatch deductions are constrained by ITA ss.18.4-18.6 and Part VI.1, and no election is available to override those matching rules for import-of-IP or reverse-hybrid structures.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Federal Goods and Services Tax (GST) in Alberta; Alberta imposes no Harmonized Sales Tax (HST) and no provincial retail sales tax, so the applicable indirect tax on taxable supplies made in Alberta is the federal GST at 5%.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in annual worldwide taxable supplies (the CRA small-supplier threshold under ETA s.148); a non-resident supplier making taxable supplies in Canada ceases to be a small supplier once worldwide gross revenue exceeds CAD 30,000, which triggers mandatory GST/HST registration under ETA s.240; voluntary registration is nevertheless available to the exporter to support input tax credit recovery and the application of the 0% export rate.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada currently imposes no real-time fiscal clearance, no mandatory fiscal API, and no digital stamping for GST/HST invoices; electronic invoicing is permitted and is being aligned on a voluntary basis with the Pan-Canadian E-Invoicing Standard (PEPPOL BIS 3.0) adopted through the Digital Governance Council; all GST/HST registrants must file returns electronically (GST/HST NETFILE), and invoices and export records must be retained in an accessible readable format for at least six years; exports must be reported to CBSA through the Canadian Export Reporting System (G-13) or an approved service provider, but no tax-authority pre-approval or digital clearance seal is required before export.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of the Color Doppler Ultrasound Console (ISIC 3250 / NAICS 334510) are zero-rated at 0% GST under ETA Schedule VI, Part V, Item 1 (supply of goods exported from Canada). To claim the zero rate, the supplier must: (i) sell the goods under a written export contract with a non-resident purchaser, (ii) physically ship the goods to a destination outside Canada, and (iii) hold contemporaneous documentary evidence of export within the two-year period mandated by ETA s.169(4). Where the console qualifies as a medical device for human use under the Medical Devices Regulations, domestic supplies to qualifying hospitals and healthcare institutions may also qualify for zero-rating under Schedule VI, Part II; however, for cross-border sales the Part V export zero-rating route governs.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canada Export Declaration (G-13 / CBSA Canadian Export Reporting System) containing the applicable Canadian Export Code for diagnostic imaging equipment
Commercial Invoice with export contract value, Incoterms, and a clear description of the Color Doppler Ultrasound Console
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / Cargo Control Document evidencing physical departure of the goods from Canada
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT MT103 bank credit advice evidencing receipt of foreign exchange from the overseas buyer
Health Canada Medical Device Establishment Licence (MDEL) or export permit where the ultrasound console is controlled as a medical device
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA scrutinizes zero-rated export claims through the Exports Verification Program and cross-checks customs declarations through CBSA. If export substantiation fails within the ETA s.169(4) two-year period, CRA deems the supply taxable at 5% GST, reassesses the unremitted tax with daily interest under ETA s.280, and claws back the input tax credits (ITCs) apportioned to the export; a gross-negligence penalty equal to 25% of the assessed tax amount (minimum CAD 250) applies under ETA s.285.1; knowingly false export documentation also exposes the exporter to penalties under ETA s.296 and criminal prosecution for tax evasion under Criminal Code s.380. Failure to repatriate export proceeds within a commercially reasonable period (benchmarked at 180 days) may lead CRA to recharacterize the foreign receivable for income tax purposes, with transfer-pricing reassessment under ITA s.247(3) and associated adjustment penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) as monetary and systemic authority; Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) as prudential regulator for Schedule I/II banks; Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) as AML/ATF supervisor under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA). No dedicated Foreign Exchange Administration exists; exchange-rate and capital-flow policy is coordinated by the Department of Finance Canada under Canada's freely floating CAD regime.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full Article VIII IMF convertibility on both current and capital accounts. Profit remittance (dividends, interest, royalties, management fees) is unrestricted and requires no Bank of Canada authorization; the only statutory gate is Part XIII non-resident withholding tax under the Income Tax Act (25% statutory, treaty-reduced to 5%–15% on dividends and typically 10%–15% on interest and royalties), administered via NR4 reporting and NR301/NR302 treaty forms. No foreign-investment review under the Investment Canada Act applies to this medical-device manufacturing scope, no minimum holding periods bind capital accounts, and foreign-currency balances may be held freely with domestic authorized banks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no statutory surrender, repatriation timeline, or mandatory conversion ratio for export proceeds. Exporters may retain USD or other currencies in domestic or foreign bank accounts indefinitely. Compliance obligations are limited to: (i) documentary evidence retention under income and sales tax rules; (ii) Export and Import Permits Act (EIPA) licensing and destination screening where the buyer is sanctioned or the technology is controlled; and (iii) Statistics Canada export reporting for shipments above CAD 2,000. Medical imaging devices additionally require a Health Canada Medical Device Establishment Licence (MDEL) attesting to compliance with the Food and Drugs Act.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (dual CAD/USD) / Capital Escrow Account for subscription funds
Operational Account (CAD and USD) with SWIFT gpi and LC services
Operational Account / Capital Escrow Account with dedicated trade finance desk
Operational Account (CAD/USD) and FX forwards margin account
Operational Account with Latin America/Caribbean correspondent emphasis
Operational Account (Provincial Crown, Alberta-focused) / Escrow Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM. Canada has no 'Electronic Money Institution' licence; foreign digital EMIs cannot access the Large Value Transfer System (LVTS) or Payments Canada clearing membership directly. An offshore EMI may operate through a sponsoring Schedule I bank (banking-as-a-service) or register as a money-service business (MSB) with FINTRAC for money transmission, but cannot take deposits or settle CAD. For this exporter, a direct Schedule I bank relationship is legally and operationally superior; the EMI channel is acceptable solely for ancillary receivables collection or merchant acquiring if FINTRAC MSB registration and Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA) payment-service registration with the Bank of Canada are in place.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Canadian Schedule I banks require at least one director, officer, or authorized signatory to attend a physical KYC interview at a Canadian branch (Calgary or Edmonton) before account activation, particularly where non-resident UBOs control the Alberta corporation. FINTRAC permits non-face-to-face verification under an enhanced two-document rule, but bank risk policies almost always override this for foreign-owned entities. Remote account opening is possible on a case-by-case basis with certified corporate documents and a pre-existing banking relationship, but the industry standard is a single physical visit after which all standing instructions may be exercised remotely.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial owners without verifiable Canadian-source wealth or economic nexus
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Government-issued passports and proof of residence; three years of audited financial statements; professional banker or legal reference from the UBO's home jurisdiction; completed source-of-wealth questionnaire; certified corporate register and share-subscription ledger showing the exact funding trail.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions / end-use concern on exports of phased-array ultrasound consoles to foreign healthcare distributors
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Health Canada Medical Device Establishment Licence (MDEL); Global Affairs Canada export screening confirmation under the EIPA; end-user certificates and healthcare installation letters of intent; denial-list and consolidated sanctions screening report; formal written Export Compliance Program policy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between declared low-risk manufacturing activity and large, frequent cross-border wires
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master supply agreements and purchase orders; pro-forma invoices; bills of lading or airway bills; HS classification notes (HS 9018.12/9018.13); confirmed commercial LC copies; annual revenue forecast matching projected account velocity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid inbound capital injection from an offshore parent during the incorporation window triggering FINTRAC large-transaction reports (CAD 10,000+)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Alberta certificate of incorporation and corporate registry extract; board resolution authorizing share issuance; executed share-subscription agreement; bank-to-bank funding reference; source-of-funds statement and foreign-exchange conversion trade ticket; FINTRAC disclosure package prepared by Canadian counsel.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: SWIFT MT103 from the parent or investor bank: Field 50K (ordering customer), Field 59 (beneficiary: Alberta corporation with account and full legal name), Field 70 (remittance information carrying ISO 20022 purpose code 'INVS' or the text 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION', Alberta registration number, and share-subscription reference), Field 71A details. CAD settlement is final on LVTS; USD settlement arrives via the Canadian bank's U.S. correspondent (Fedwire/CHIPS). Canadian receiving banks apply FINTRAC large-transaction reporting at CAD 10,000 or equivalent and require a Pre-Arrival Notification for incoming international wires exceeding CAD 100,000. No exchange-control authorization is required; documentary evidence supports the underlying share issuance for tax and audit purposes.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Settlement rails: (i) irrevocable Commercial Letters of Credit issued via SWIFT MT700, advised or confirmed in the buyer's jurisdiction, utilized against UCP600-compliant documents; (ii) SWIFT MT103/TT wires for open-account payments with SWIFT gpi end-to-end tracking; (iii) documentary collections (D/P and D/A) under URC522 for distributor markets. CAD outbounds settle with finality on LVTS; USD outbounds clear through the U.S. correspondent network. The configured target rails (Swift_LC and TT_Wire) are fully supported without supplementary licensing.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CAD/USD vanilla FX forwards (1–24 months) with Schedule I dealers; no underlying balance-sheet exposure test required
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (XCCY CAD/USD) under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement and CSA for long-term intercompany loan and asset-lifetime currency risk
European-style FX options and zero-premium collar structures to hedge order-specific or tender-driven USD price exposure
Exchange-traded FX futures and options on the Montréal Exchange (MX) providing cleared, margined hedging exposure

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs): legally permitted, but commercially non-standard; CAD is fully deliverable and convertible, so NDFs are quoted only for exotic crosses and are not recommended for this entity

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each anniversary of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file is a corporate offence; continued default may allow the Registrar to administratively dissolve the corporation. Restoration requires filing all missing returns plus applicable penalties and restoration fees.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return and Alberta Corporate Tax Return filed jointly with the Canada Revenue Agency
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency under the Federal-Provincial Tax Collection Agreement for Alberta
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the corporation's fiscal year-end; balance-due payment is generally due 2 months after year-end, with a 3-month period for qualifying Canadian-controlled private corporations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty is 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month up to 12 months, and interest accrues daily. Continued non-filing may trigger CRA compliance action and director liability for unremitted source deductions or GST/HST.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No revenue-based compulsory audit applies to a private Alberta business corporation. An auditor must be appointed at each annual meeting unless all voting shareholders waive the auditor appointment; an audit is mandatory for reporting issuers, if shareholders validly require it, or if lenders or regulators require audited financial statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Publicly accountable and reporting enterprises must apply IFRS. Private Alberta corporations may use IFRS or Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE). Corporate income tax reporting is based on accounting income reconciled to taxable income under the Income Tax Act.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The corporation must maintain an internal Individuals with Significant Control (ISC) register and update it within 15 days after any share transfer or change in significant control. At each fiscal year-end, the directors should confirm the ISC register is accurate. Alberta does not require a separate public UBO annual filing; the Alberta Annual Return captures only registered office, directors, and officer information.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control (UBO register)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 180 – 500 per annum for Alberta registered office and registered agent services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 12,000 – 35,000 per full audit for a private medical device manufacturer with moderate transaction volume; a review engagement is typically USD 5,000 – 12,000 if audit is waived

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 23.0% combined general rate (15.0% federal Part I after provincial abatement + 8.0% Alberta general rate); 11.0% combined small business rate for a CCPC on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income (9.0% federal + 2.0% Alberta)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No sector-specific tax holiday for ISIC 3250 medical device manufacturers. Federal SR&ED investment tax credits: 35% refundable credit for CCPCs on up to CAD 3,000,000 of eligible expenditures; 15% non-refundable credit for other corporations. Accelerated capital cost allowance under CCA Classes 29 (manufacturing/processing) and 43.1/43.2 (clean energy). Alberta Investor Tax Credit (30% for eligible venture investments) and Alberta Innovation Employment Grant may reduce effective provincial cost; export grants do not alter the CIT rate.
